title: Access governance orchestration and signed export manifests for cross-region compliance
creator: Maya Chen
description: Problem: Enterprise customers require a reproducible, auditable package that proves who had access to tenant data, where that data resided, and how long artifacts were retained. Current ad-hoc exports are manual, inconsistent across regions, and lack cryptographic integrity checks or SCIM/RBAC reconciliation artifacts.
acceptance_criteria: Automated daily exports of access evidence per tenant and per region into a customer-specified, encrypted S3 bucket (or equivalent) with tenancy metadata
Exports include: user->role mappings at snapshot time, SCIM provisioning events for the day, SSO/SAML login events (with masked PII), account-level policy versions, and associated retention settings
Each export is accompanied by a signed manifest (ed25519) and export checksum; signatures are verifiable with our published public key
System demonstrates retention-aware exports: objects older than tenant retention policy are excluded and an exclusion report is produced
On-demand export API for compliance reviewers that can generate a one-off evidence package for a given date range
Periodic access-review trigger: system will generate a candidate reviewer list and delta report (added/removed privileged principals) to drive human reviews
SCIM reconciliation job reports mismatches (e.g., groups present in SCIM but missing RBAC bindings) and creates actionable tickets via GitHub API integration
All exported artifacts include region and data residency tags so a customer can demonstrate that access evidence for EU tenants stays within EU-resident storages when requested
implementation_notes: Design a lightweight export orchestration microservice that composes artifacts from audit-log-store, RBAC store, SCIM events index, and SSO auth logs
Export format: gzipped tarball with the following structure: /manifest.json, /rbac_snapshot.jsonl, /scim_events.jsonl, /sso_events.jsonl (PII redacted), /retention_report.json
Manifests must include ISO-8601 timestamps, region, tenant_id, export_version, and the ed25519 signature over the manifest plus file checksums

Reconciliation workflow: 1) compute SCIM group vs RBAC binding set differences, 2) mark discrepancies as severity levels, 3) create GitHub issue with reproducible repro (query links) and put into a "scim-recon" repo label

For data residency, use regional export workers that only stage artifacts in region-specific encrypted buckets; central orchestrator only holds pointers and never copies raw artifacts across residency boundaries
Retention enforcement: export pipeline should consult tenant.retention_policy and drop/flag items excluded by retention (and log reason codes). Export should surface retention rules version used
SSO/SAML: ensure session revocation events are captured; provide a compact delta of active sessions at snapshot time to show who could have accessed resources
Operational metrics: export success rate, time-to-generate, size per tenant, number of reconciliation mismatches, signature verification failures

Privacy: PII redaction for sso_events.jsonl must be deterministic but reversible for internal SRE if subpoena workflow invoked; design a HSM-backed reversible tokenization plan (requires legal/ops signoff)

Cross-region export tooling: infra quota for creating region-specific export buckets requires approvals from infra team
